name: White Mountain National Forest
blurb: Moose, hares and fir forest below a windswept alpine peak.

tip.title: Lose the snowshoe hare
tip.text: Hares are the main prey of fishers and are also taken by bobcats and coyotes. Set Snowshoe hare to -100% and watch fisher, marten and bobcat, then the fir and bunchberry it browses.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A cold-climate conifer of the northern forest and a browse plant for hare, deer and beaver in GloBI feeding records.
A hardwood of the lower forest. Its leaves, twigs and nuts are eaten by hare, deer, beaver, mice and bears.
A small understory tree. Moose browse its new growth, and a GloBI record links the two.

nodes.name: Bunchberry
nodes.desc: A common forest-floor plant of the cool woods, eaten by hare, voles and bears in GloBI records.
A large browser of young shoots and twigs. Winter ticks, helped by milder winters, have driven moose declines in New Hampshire.
Browses twigs, buds and plants in the forest and is hunted by bobcats and coyotes.
Browses conifer and shrub shoots. It is the main prey of the fisher.
Fells trees and eats bark and twigs of fir and beech, building ponds that make wetland habitat.
A small plant-eater of wet meadows and forest edges, and prey for many carnivores.
Eats seeds, nuts and plant matter, and is common prey for snakes, bobcats and coyotes.
A tiny predator of small animals. GloBI records show it eating voles and snakes.
Eats frogs, small mammals and amphibians, based on GloBI records.
A forest weasel that hunts small mammals and hares, and is itself killed by fishers and bobcats.
A generalist hunter whose main prey are snowshoe hares and porcupines. It also eats small mammals and carrion.
A cat that preys on hares, rodents and deer, and also takes marten and fisher.
An adaptable predator and scavenger of hares, rodents and the carcasses of deer and moose.
An omnivore that eats berries, beech nuts and plants, and takes beaver, hare and young moose.
Short, cool growing seasons limit plant growth in the mountains.
Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
